Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment focuses on identifying N-terminal cleavage products of Cyclophilin D using in-gel digestion and DDA LC-MS/MS. While the paper discusses PTMs (phosphorylation, acetylation) and uses a SUMO tag for recombinant protein expression, the actual mass spectrometry analysis described for the sample identification was a standard bottom-up DDA approach on excised gel bands. Iodoacetamide was used for alkylation, which is a standard sample prep step.

scope: The bands of interest were excised, destained by 3 min incubation with acetonitrile for three times and then left to dry on air.

Recombinant FL-CyPD and ΔN-CyPD displayed almost identical CsA-sensitive PPIase activity as determined by refolding of RNase T1 (Fig. 1d), clearly indicating that the NTT is not necessary for the catalytic activity. We could resolve FL-CyPD and ΔN-CyPD in 15% SDS-PAGE gels and confirmed their identity by mass spectrometry (Fig. 1c).
The two bands at 19 kDa and 18 kDa were manually excised from SDS-PAGE for mass spectrometry analysis.
